proposals.before: His father Gunazan served the Taizong. On the campaign against the Ming, below Datong he stormed Little Stone City and was first over the wall. He was granted the title "Baturu" and a hereditary rank as niru janggin.
proposals.after: His father Gunazan served the Taizong. On the campaign against the Ming, when the army halted at Datong, he stormed Little Stone City and was first over the wall. He was granted the title "Baturu" and a hereditary rank as niru janggin.
proposals.reason: Chinese 次大同 means the army halted or encamped at Datong, not that the assault occurred below Datong.

proposals.before: Governor Fu Honglie was defeated by Wu Sangui's general Wu Shijiong, and Manggitu marched to join forces with him.
proposals.after: Governor Fu Honglie was defeated by Wu Sangui's general Wu Shicong, and Manggitu marched to join forces with him.
proposals.reason: Chinese 吳世琮 uses 琮 (cóng), not a graph read Shijiong; the personal name should be Shicong.

proposals.before: The army advanced and took Nanning. The rebel Ma Chengzhao united with Wu Sangui's troops to some one hundred thousand men and offered battle.
proposals.after: The army advanced and took Nanning. The rebel Ma Chengyin united with Wu Sangui's troops to some one hundred thousand men and offered battle.
proposals.reason: Chinese 馬承廕 uses 廕 (yìn); Chengzhao is a mistranscription of Chengyin.

proposals.before: In year 19 Manggitu died in camp. Gu Badai followed Pacification of the South Grand General Ceben south into Yunnan to besiege the provincial capital.
proposals.after: In year 19 Manggitu died in camp. Gu Badai followed Pacification of the South Grand General Laita south into Yunnan to besiege the provincial capital.
proposals.reason: Chinese 賚塔 is Laita; Ceben does not match the characters.

proposals.before: Gansu Provincial Commander Zhang Yong asked to slow the advance; the emperor ordered Tulai to hold the passes at Fengxiang, Qinzhou, and other key points, detach troops to Pacification of the South General Muzhan's descent on Huguang, and ordered Ma Erhan to follow.
proposals.after: Gansu Provincial Commander Zhang Yong asked to slow the advance; the emperor ordered Tulai to hold the passes at Fengxiang, Qinzhou, and other key points, detach troops to Conquest-the-South General Muzhan's descent on Huguang, and ordered Ma Erhan to follow.
proposals.reason: 征南將軍 is a campaign title 'General who campaigns south', not 平南 'Pacification of the South'.

proposals.before: In year 26 he was appointed Director of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
proposals.after: In year 26 he was appointed Secretary of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
proposals.reason: 司務 is a secretaryship in the Court of Colonial Affairs, not the director-level office implied by English Director.

proposals.before: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Director of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
proposals.after: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Secretary of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
proposals.reason: 司務 is a secretaryship in the Court of Colonial Affairs, not the director-level office implied by English Director.

proposals.before: He was promoted again to Minister of War, made a lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and named a Grand Councilor.
proposals.after: He was promoted again to Minister of War, made a lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and named a Deliberative Minister.
proposals.reason: 議政大臣 is a minister of the Deliberative Council, not a Grand Councilor (軍機大臣).

proposals.before: He was again promoted to Minister of War, appointed lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and enrolled among the Grand Councilors.
proposals.after: He was again promoted to Minister of War, appointed lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and enrolled among the Deliberative Ministers.
proposals.reason: 議政大臣 is a minister of the Deliberative Council, not a Grand Councilor (軍機大臣).

proposals.before: In Kangxi year 35 the emperor campaigned in person against Galdan and stationed Ma Erhan at Tumubao to manage relay posts. Because the army horses supplied were in poor condition, the personnel office recommended dismissal, but the emperor showed leniency.
proposals.after: In Kangxi year 35 the emperor campaigned in person against Galdan and stationed Ma Erhan at Tumu to manage relay posts. Because the army horses supplied were in poor condition, the personnel office recommended dismissal, but the emperor showed leniency.
proposals.reason: 土木 is Tumu; Tumubao invents a fortified-place reading not required by the Chinese.

proposals.before: In the thirty-fifth year the emperor campaigned in person against Galdan and ordered Ma Erhan to remain at Tumubao to oversee relay stations; because the army horses sent were weak, the personnel office recommended stripping his office, but the emperor ordered leniency.
proposals.after: In the thirty-fifth year the emperor campaigned in person against Galdan and ordered Ma Erhan to remain at Tumu to oversee relay stations; because the army horses sent were weak, the personnel office recommended stripping his office, but the emperor ordered leniency.
proposals.reason: 土木 is Tumu; Tumubao invents a fortified-place reading not required by the Chinese.

proposals.before: He memorialized, "At home I read the imperial edict clearing Suksaha, whom Oboi destroyed out of enmity, killing his sons and grandsons and implicating Bai'erhetu's clan by association.
proposals.after: He memorialized, "At home I read the imperial edict clearing Suksaha, whom Oboi destroyed out of enmity, killing his sons and grandsons and implicating the clansman Bai'erhetu by association.
proposals.reason: Chinese 連坐族人白爾赫圖 names Bai'erhetu as the implicated clansman, not a collective 'clan of Bai'erhetu'.

proposals.before: He memorialized: "At home I read the imperial edict clearing Suksaha, who was framed and destroyed by Oboi out of enmity, killing his sons and grandsons and implicating the clan of Bai'erhetu by association.
proposals.after: He memorialized: "At home I read the imperial edict clearing Suksaha, who was framed and destroyed by Oboi out of enmity, killing his sons and grandsons and implicating the clansman Bai'erhetu by association.
proposals.reason: Chinese 族人白爾赫圖 is the kinsman Bai'erhetu, not Bai'erhetu's clan as a group.

proposals.before: He was transferred to Intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.
proposals.after: He was transferred to Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
proposals.reason: 順天府尹 is the prefect (yin) of Shuntian, not an intendant.

proposals.before: He was transferred to Intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.
proposals.after: He was transferred to Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
proposals.reason: 府尹 is prefect of the metropolitan prefecture, not intendant.

proposals.before: Jin Shengzong rebelled in Jiangxi and Jiang Xian in Datong—no different from Geng Jingzhong and Wang Fuchen.
proposals.after: Jin Shenghuan rebelled in Jiangxi and Jiang Xiang in Datong—no different from Geng Jingzhong and Wang Fuchen.
proposals.reason: 金聲桓 is Jin Shenghuan, not Shengzong; 姜瓖 is Jiang Xiang, not Xian.

proposals.before: Jin Shengzong rebelled in Jiangxi and Jiang Xian in Datong—no different from Geng Jingzhong and Wang Fuchen.
proposals.after: Jin Shenghuan rebelled in Jiangxi and Jiang Xiang in Datong—no different from Geng Jingzhong and Wang Fuchen.
proposals.reason: The characters 聲桓 and 瓖 do not support the English spellings Shengzong and Xian.

proposals.before: Circuit intendants pay annual gifts to prefects, who add exactions on top, so the officials and people under a prefect are virtually sold to him.
proposals.after: Circuits and prefectures pay annual customary gifts, and with additional squeezing the officials and people under them are virtually sold to those circuits and prefectures.
proposals.reason: 道府歲納規禮 names circuits and prefectures as the payers of customary gifts, not circuit intendants paying prefects; the sold subjects are those under 道府.

proposals.before: Circuit intendants pay annual customary gifts to prefects, who add exactions on top, so the officials and people under a prefect are no better than sold to the prefect.
proposals.after: Circuits and prefectures pay annual customary gifts, and with additional squeezing the officials and people under the circuits and prefectures are no better than sold to them.
proposals.reason: The literal reverses 道府 as payers into a circuit-to-prefect gift, which the Chinese does not say.

proposals.before: Prefectures and counties pay annual gifts to circuit intendants, who add extortion on top, so the gentry and people under a county are virtually sold to it.
proposals.after: Departments and counties pay annual customary gifts, and with further extortion the gentry and people under them are virtually sold to those departments and counties.
proposals.reason: 州縣歲納規禮 does not state that prefectures pay circuit intendants; the victims are 州縣所屬士民 sold to the 州縣.

proposals.before: Prefectures and counties pay annual gifts to circuit intendants, who add extortion on top, so the gentry and people under a county are no better than sold to the county.
proposals.after: Departments and counties pay annual customary gifts, and with further extortion the gentry and people belonging to them are no better than sold to the departments and counties.
proposals.reason: The added 'to circuit intendants' is not in 州縣歲納規禮.

proposals.before: In the Shunzhi reign, Shandong surveillance commissioner Cheng Heng impeached Governor Geng Tun, and Jiangnan surveillance commissioner Qin Shizhen impeached Tu Guobao—both received heavy punishment, and the empire was awed.
proposals.after: In the Shunzhi reign, Shandong regional inspector Cheng Heng impeached Governor Geng Tun, and Jiangnan regional inspector Qin Shizhen impeached Tu Guobao—both received heavy punishment, and the empire was awed.
proposals.reason: 巡按 is the regional inspector, not the surveillance commissioner (按察使).

proposals.before: In the Shizu reign, Shandong Surveillance Commissioner Cheng Heng impeached Governor Geng Tun, and Jiangnan Surveillance Commissioner Qin Shizhen impeached Tu Guobao—both received heavy punishment, and all under Heaven were awed.
proposals.after: In the Shizu reign, Shandong Regional Inspector Cheng Heng impeached Governor Geng Tun, and Jiangnan Regional Inspector Qin Shizhen impeached Tu Guobao—both received heavy punishment, and all under Heaven were awed.
proposals.reason: 巡按 should be rendered Regional Inspector rather than Surveillance Commissioner.

proposals.before: When Kinmen and Xiamen were pacified, Governor Yao Qisheng asked that land beyond the boundary be returned by household register, maritime prohibitions relaxed, and profits from fish and salt used for military supplies; court ministers opposed it.
proposals.after: When Kinmen and Xiamen were pacified, Governor-General Yao Qisheng asked that land beyond the boundary be returned by household register, maritime prohibitions relaxed, and profits from fish and salt used for military supplies; court ministers opposed it.
proposals.reason: Chinese 總督 is governor-general, not the lower office rendered as Governor.

proposals.before: After they arrived, Wu Sangui plotted rebellion. Provincial Commander Li Benshen joined the plot and wrote to recruit Guizhou Governor Cao Shenji. Governor-General Gan Wenxuan learned of it, informed Sa Muha and the others, urged them to hurry to the capital to report the rebellion, and asked for relief troops.
proposals.after: After they arrived, Wu Sangui plotted rebellion. Provincial Commander Li Benshen joined the plot and wrote to recruit Guizhou Governor Cao Shenji. Governor-General Gan Wenkun learned of it, informed Sa Muha and the others, urged them to hurry to the capital to report the rebellion, and asked for relief troops.
proposals.reason: The given name 焜 is Kun, not Xuan; English Gan Wenxuan mismatches the Chinese.

proposals.before: In year 14, in accounting merit for reporting the rebellion, Sa Muha, Dangwuli, and Xilantai were all due for promotion to minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and similar posts.
proposals.after: In year 14, in accounting merit for reporting the rebellion, Sa Muha, Dangwuli, and Xilantai were all due for promotion to minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and similar posts.
proposals.reason: Guanglu si (光祿) is the Court of Imperial Entertainments, not the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

proposals.before: Before long Bin entered service as Minister and memorialized, "The sea mouth need not be dredged urgently; if flood comes again, downstream prefectures and counties will all be submerged."
proposals.after: Before long Bin entered service as Minister and memorialized, "If the sea mouth is not dredged promptly, should flood come again, the downstream prefectures and counties will all be submerged."
proposals.reason: Chinese 海口不急濬 is a conditional ('if the sea mouth is not urgently dredged'), not a recommendation that dredging is unnecessary; the following 再遇水 clause is the consequence of that failure.

proposals.before: Before long Bin entered service as Minister and memorialized: "The sea mouth need not be dredged urgently; if water comes again, the downstream prefectures and counties will all be given to vast flooding."
proposals.after: Before long Bin entered service as Minister and memorialized: "If the sea mouth is not urgently dredged, should water come again, the downstream prefectures and counties will all be given over to vast flooding."
proposals.reason: The literal likewise inverts 不急濬 from a negative condition into 'need not be dredged,' reversing Tang Bin's warning.

claimRevisions.reason: The English personal name must follow 吳世琮 as Wu Shicong, not Wu Shijiong.
The English personal name must follow 馬承廕 as Ma Chengyin, not Ma Chengzhao.
The English personal name must follow 賚塔 as Laita, not Ceben.
The title 征南將軍 is General Who Campaigns South, not Pacification of the South or the awkward Conquest-the-South calque.
The English personal name must follow 金聲桓 as Jin Shenghuan, not Jin Shengzong.
The English personal name must follow 姜瓖 as Jiang Xiang, not Jiang Xian.
The title claim must render 總督 as Governor-General, not Governor.
The English and pinyin must follow 甘文焜 as Gan Wenkun, not Gan Wenxuan.
The title string must use Gan Wenkun for 甘文焜.
